title: Realtime multiplayer, automation, and you! — Idan Gazit, GitHub
talk_summary: Idan Gazit demos two GitHub Next prototypes: Agentic Workflows (markdown-authored background automations with deterministic YAML guardrails and safe-outputs) and Ace (cloud microVM multiplayer dev sessions where agents read chat backscroll and shared plan documents). The transferable core is guardrail design for unsupervised agents and treating markdown plans as the shared source of truth.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic guardrails outside the prompt, not in it
takeaways.what_they_do: Permissions, allowed tools, allowed network hosts, and allowed write actions are declared in YAML front matter compiled into the workflow, so a prompt-injected agent cannot escalate beyond them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you're prompting the guardrails at the agent, you're effectively letting the fox loose in the henhouse

takeaways.technique: Secrets held by a warden, never visible to the agent
takeaways.what_they_do: Secrets live outside the agent's sandbox; the agent requests a brokered call and the warden performs it, so the agent never sees the credential.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If an agent can know a secret, that secret, you need to treat it as if it's already been compromised.

takeaways.what_they_do: The workflow declares exactly which write actions are permitted (e.g. create at most one PR) and explicitly permits no-op, so background agents don't generate noise or denial-of-service.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I explicitly said you're allowed to do nothing... the last thing I want is noise

takeaways.technique: Markdown plan as the shared, editable source of truth
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents emit plans as markdown docs that humans and agents co-edit; the agent then executes 'make the document true' rather than re-deriving intent from chat.
takeaways.evidence_quote: in order to change something about my application, I'm going to edit a document, and I'm going to tell AI, 'Hey, make the document true.'

takeaways.technique: Agents consume conversation backscroll to resolve final intent
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent reads the full human discussion and extracts the settled decision from messy back-and-forth, so users don't restate instructions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: AI is also really good at fishing out that final state... I don't need to work for the robots.

takeaways.technique: Every session is a cloud microVM branch, nothing on the host
takeaways.what_they_do: Each dev session is a repo branch checked out into a cloud microVM, so heavy builds and dev servers never touch the local/host machine.
takeaways.evidence_quote: none of this is running on my machine. It's all micro VMs in the cloud.
